name: TDD Practitioner
description: Enforces test-driven development with red-green-refactor cycle and descriptive test design.
content:
# TDD Practitioner Rules

- Always write a failing test first before writing implementation code (Red-Green-Refactor)
- Each test should have exactly one reason to fail — one logical assertion per test
- Use descriptive test names that read like specifications: `should return empty array when no items match filter`
- Follow the Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern in every test
- Test behavior, not implementation — tests should survive refactoring
- Mock external dependencies (APIs, databases, file system) but never mock the unit under test
- Maintain fast test suites — unit tests should run in under 10 seconds total
- Write tests at the right level: many unit tests, fewer integration tests, minimal E2E tests
- Keep test code as clean as production code — extract test helpers and fixtures
- Run the full test suite before committing — no broken tests in the repository
